eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus has converged at 100% implied probability on a daily maximum of exactly 21°C for Helsinki on August 21, 2026, driven by real-time surface observations and short-range forecast guidance aligning on that peak.** 

Official station data from Helsinki-Vantaa Airport (EFHK) and nearby sites such as Kaisaniemi recorded afternoon temperatures reaching 19–20°C under mostly clear to partly cloudy skies with light southwesterly flow, while ensemble and deterministic models (including GFS and ECMWF guidance referenced in public forecasts) consistently projected a ceiling near 20–21°C before cooling set in during the evening. This places the expected high modestly above the 1991–2020 climatological average of 19.8°C for the date but well below historical extremes exceeding 26°C. 

The near-certainty reflects the advanced stage of the diurnal cycle on the resolution date, with limited remaining potential for significant additional warming. 

Realistic challenges include post-observation quality-control revisions at the primary reporting station, use of a different official site for market settlement, or localized microclimate effects not captured in the broader forecast.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from the Korea Meteorological Administration indicate a high near 28–29°C for Incheon on August 22, with possible thundershowers and overcast skies limiting peak solar heating. Late-August climatology shows seasonal cooling from the North Pacific High's influence, with typical maxima declining from 31°C mid-month toward 27–29°C; coastal moderation at Incheon and urban effects in Seoul add minor variability. Model consensus favors these outcomes over 30°C+ because precipitation probability around 20–60% reduces daytime warming, while 27°C or lower would require stronger cloud cover or earlier frontal passage than current runs suggest. Trader sentiment reflects this narrow range of uncertainty ahead of final observational data.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Austin-Bergstrom International Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 22 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Austin-Bergstrom International Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/us/tx/austin/KAUS.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Current National Weather Service and AccuWeather guidance places Austin’s August 22 high near 105 °F under continued high-pressure ridging, low humidity, and mostly sunny skies, aligning with the market’s 52 % implied probability on 104–105 °F. Recent model runs show limited spread around this value, with ensemble means holding in the 103–106 °F band; only modest steering-flow changes or unexpected cloud cover would shift the outcome into the 102–103 °F or 106–107 °F bins that together command another 44.5 % of trader capital. Historical August climatology (average high ~97 °F) underscores how persistent late-summer ridging has elevated baseline temperatures, yet the narrow forecast uncertainty keeps probabilities tightly clustered near the 104–106 °F range ahead of tomorrow’s official high.

This market will resolve based on the highest temperature recorded in the 'Daily Observations' table on Weather Underground, not the figure displayed in the 'Day High & Low' summary section; in the event of any discrepancy between the two, the Daily Observations table shall be the primary resolution source not the Day High & Low section.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded at the Masroor Airbase Station in degrees Celsius on 23 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Masroor Airbase Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/pk/karachi/OPKC.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple models and PAGASA indicate Manila's August 23 high will likely reach 30–31°C amid the southwest monsoon, which sustains widespread cloud cover, high humidity near 80%, and scattered thunderstorms that reduce solar heating. These conditions align with historical August averages of 30–31°C and explain the tight market clustering around those outcomes, as stronger or earlier convection could cap the peak near 29°C while clearer breaks might allow brief warming to 32°C. Official monitoring of monsoon strength and local convective timing through the weekend will provide the key updates influencing final resolution.
